name: Italian Game
description: A practical 1.e4 course that starts with the classic Italian setup, then teaches simple responses to common Black defenses.

branches.title: Main Line: Italian Setup
branches.description: Learn the default beginner Italian setup before studying deviations.

moves.title: Claim the center
moves.explanation: Controls d5 and f5, opens the bishop and queen, and starts the game by fighting for central space instead of making a slow side move.

moves.title: Black mirrors the center
moves.explanation: Black also fights for central space. This creates an open position where quick development matters.

moves.title: Develop with a threat
moves.explanation: Develops a knight, attacks e5, and prepares castling. This avoids the beginner mistake of bringing the queen out too early.

moves.title: Black defends e5
moves.explanation: Black develops while defending the e5 pawn. White should continue improving pieces, not chase pawns.

moves.title: Point at f7
moves.explanation: Develops the bishop to an active diagonal, prepares castling, and creates natural pressure on f7 without forcing an attack too soon.

hints: The target response in this branch is Bc4.
Use the highlighted move and keep the plan simple.

branches.title: Sicilian Defense Response
branches.description: If Black answers e4 with c5, stay calm and develop naturally.

moves.title: Start with e4
moves.explanation: White takes central space and invites Black to show their setup.

moves.title: Black plays the Sicilian
moves.explanation: This is the Sicilian Defense. Black attacks d4 from the side instead of copying e5.

moves.title: Recommended: develop Nf3
moves.explanation: Nf3 develops, supports central play, and keeps White flexible. The beginner goal is development and king safety, not an immediate attack.

hints: The target response in this branch is Nf3.

branches.title: Caro-Kann Response
branches.description: If Black prepares d5 with c6, build a strong center.

moves.title: Start with e4
moves.explanation: White controls the center and opens lines.

moves.title: Black plays the Caro-Kann
moves.explanation: Black prepares d5 with support. This is solid and aims to challenge your center next.

moves.title: Recommended: build the center
moves.explanation: d4 creates a strong pawn duo and meets Black's plan directly. Develop pieces next instead of chasing tricks.

hints: The target response in this branch is d4.
Use the highlighted move and keep the plan simple.

branches.title: French Defense Response
branches.description: If Black prepares d5 with e6, take space and develop calmly.

moves.title: Start with e4
moves.explanation: White controls central squares and opens piece lines.

moves.title: Black plays the French
moves.explanation: Black prepares d5 and accepts a slightly closed structure.

moves.title: Recommended: occupy the center
moves.explanation: d4 takes space before Black challenges it. The plan is develop, support the center, and avoid premature pawn storms.

hints: The target response in this branch is d4.
Use the highlighted move and keep the plan simple.

branches.title: Scandinavian Response
branches.description: If Black strikes immediately with d5, capture once and develop.

moves.title: Start with e4
moves.explanation: White claims the center.

moves.title: Black plays the Scandinavian
moves.explanation: Black directly attacks the e4 pawn and often brings the queen out after a capture.

moves.title: Recommended: capture the pawn
moves.explanation: exd5 accepts the challenge. If Black recaptures with the queen, develop with tempo and avoid chasing with random pawns.

hints: The target response in this branch is exd5.

branches.description: Replay the main Italian setup from memory.

moves.title: Center first
moves.explanation: Start with the center.

moves.title: Black mirrors
moves.explanation: Recognize the open game.

moves.title: Develop
moves.explanation: Attack e5 and prepare castling.

moves.title: Black develops
moves.explanation: Continue calmly.

moves.title: Bishop out
moves.explanation: Finish the Italian setup.

ideas: Learn the main Italian setup first.
Against c5, c6, e6, or d5, respond with center control and development.
Your goal is confidence in real beginner games, not memorizing engine lines.
commonMistakes: Panicking when Black does not play e5.
Moving the queen early instead of building pieces.
